The second is more fitting, because the meaning is "or two other just men from other than you"; this is how the meaning of آخر must be in the language, and a non-Muslim is not just. إِنْ أَنْتُمْ ضَرَبْتُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ: «أنتم» is nominative by an implied verb like the second. تَحْبِسُونَهُما مِنْ بَعْدِ الصَّلاةِ: i.e. the afternoon (ʿaṣr) prayer; it was singled out for this because there is no [voluntary] prayer after it, so people are free after it. فَيُقْسِمانِ بِاللَّهِ: meaning the two against whom the claim is made. إِنِ ارْتَبْتُمْ: parenthetical; the implied form is "so the two swear by Allah, saying: لا نَشْتَرِي بِهِ ثَمَناً", i.e. by our oath. وَلَوْ كانَ ذا قُرْبى: parenthetical, i.e. even if the deceased were a relative. وَلا نَكْتُمُ شَهادَةَ اللَّهِ: connected to His words «ثمنا». Ibn Muḥayṣin read إنّا إذا لملّاثمين, assimilating the nūn into the lām.
This is bad in Arabic, because the lām is by rule quiescent, and if it is given a vowel, the vowel belongs only to the hamza. The parallel to this is the reading of Abū ʿAmr and Nāfiʿ وإنّه أهلك عادا لولى [al-Najm: 51]. Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard Muḥammad ibn al-Walīd say: I heard Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] say: I do not know that Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ committed a solecism in anything of the core of Arabic except in two words: one is وإنّه أهلك عادا لّولى, and the other is يُؤَدِّهِ إِلَيْكَ [Āl ʿImrān: 75].

nahhas-irab:107-107.t:
فَإِنْ عُثِرَ: in the position of a jussive by the condition. From it one says: "I came upon him (ʿathartu ʿalayhi) in the sin, aʿthuru ʿuthūran", and "I stumbled (ʿathartu) in walking, aʿthuru ʿithāran". فَآخَرانِ: nominative by an implied verb. يَقُومانِ: in the position of a naʿt (adjective). مَقامَهُما: a maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being "a standing like their standing"; then the qualifier was put in place of the qualified and the muḍāf in place of the muḍāf ilayhi. مِنَ الَّذِينَ اسْتَحَقَّ عَلَيْهِمُ: it is reported from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb: مِنَ الَّذِينَ اسْتَحَقَّ with a fatḥa on the tāʾ and the ḥāʾ; and likewise Ḥafṣ ibn Sulaymān reported from ʿĀṣim ibn Abī al-Najūd.
الْأَوْلَيانِ, the reading of the people of Medina, may be a badal (substitute) for His words «فآخران», or for the latent pronoun in يَقُومانِ. It has been said: it is the noun of that whose agent is not named (nāʾib fāʿil, deputy agent), i.e. "against whom the sin of the two nearest [heirs] has become due", like وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ; and the meaning according to whoever holds this view is "of those against whom the sin has become due through the betrayal". عليهم is in the sense of فيهم, like عَلى مُلْكِ سُلَيْمانَ [al-Baqara: 102], i.e. in the kingdom of Solomon. The meaning is: the nearest to the deceased, or [the nearest] to the oath. The Kufans read الأولين, a badal for الذين or for the hāʾ and mīm in عليهم; and الأولان is reported from al-Ḥasan. فَيُقْسِمانِ بِاللَّهِ لَشَهادَتُنا أَحَقُّ مِنْ شَهادَتِهِما: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); we have mentioned what there is on it. It is more fitting that it refer to the heirs of the deceased; as for its being the two witnesses who swear, that is far-fetched. It became difficult only because of His words لشهادتنا; its explanation is that testimony is in the sense of a report, and every reporter is a witness. Maʿmar reported from Ayyūb from Ibn Sīrīn from ʿUbayda, who said: two men of the heirs of the deceased stood and swore.

nahhas-irab:108-108.t: ذلِكَ أَدْنى: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). أَنْ: in the position of an accusative. يَأْتُوا: accusative by أن. أَوْ يَخافُوا: conjoined to it. أَنْ تُرَدَّ: in the position of an accusative by يخافوا. وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَاسْمَعُوا: a command, therefore the nūn has been dropped from it. وَاللَّهُ لا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الْفاسِقِينَ: a naʿt (adjective) of القوم. فسق يفسق and يفسق, i.e. he went out from obedience to disobedience.

nahhas-irab:109-109.t: يَوْمَ يَجْمَعُ اللَّهُ الرُّسُلَ: an adverb of time, governed by واسمعوا, i.e. "and hear the report of a day". It has been said: the implied form is "and fear a day when Allah gathers the messengers". فَيَقُولُ ماذا أُجِبْتُمْ قالُوا لا عِلْمَ لَنا: the statement of Mujāhid on this — that they are terrified and say "We have no knowledge" — is not sound, because the messengers, Allah's blessings be upon them, have no fear upon them, nor do they grieve. What is correct in this is that the meaning is: "What answer did you receive, in secret and in public?", so that this is a rebuke to the disbelievers; and they say "We have no knowledge", so that this is a giving of the lie to whoever took the Messiah as a god. إِلَّا ما عَلَّمْتَنا: in the position of a nominative because it is the khabar (predicate) of the [lā of] absolute denial (tabriʾa); it may also be in the position of an accusative by exception.

nahhas-irab:110-110.t:
إِذْ قالَ اللَّهُ يا عِيسَى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ اذْكُرْ نِعْمَتِي عَلَيْكَ وَعَلى والِدَتِكَ إِذْ أَيَّدْتُكَ بِرُوحِ الْقُدُسِ تُكَلِّمُ النَّاسَ فِي الْمَهْدِ وَكَهْلاً وَإِذْ عَلَّمْتُكَ الْكِتابَ وَالْحِكْمَةَ وَالتَّوْراةَ وَالْإِنْجِيلَ وَإِذْ تَخْلُقُ مِنَ الطِّينِ كَهَيْئَةِ الطَّيْرِ بِإِذْنِي فَتَنْفُخُ فِيها فَتَكُونُ طَيْراً بِإِذْنِي وَتُبْرِئُ الْأَكْمَهَ وَالْأَبْرَصَ بِإِذْنِي وَإِذْ تُخْرِجُ الْمَوْتى بِإِذْنِي وَإِذْ كَفَفْتُ بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ عَنْكَ إِذْ جِئْتَهُمْ بِالْبَيِّناتِ فَقالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْهُمْ إِنْ هذا إِلاَّ سِحْرٌ مُبِينٌ (110) إِذْ قالَ اللَّهُ يا عِيسَى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ: it may be a single call, in which case عِيسَى, Allah's blessings be upon him, is in the position of an accusative; or it may be two calls, in which case عِيسَى, peace be upon him, is in the position of a ḍamma, and ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ
is a second vocative; or, if you wish, a badal (substitute); or, if you wish, a naʿt (adjective) according to the position. The nominative is not permissible in the second when it is a muḍāf (in a construct), except according to al-Ṭuwāl, who permitted the nominative. Ibn Muḥayṣin read إذ آيدتك, and so it is reported from Mujāhid, and so al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī al-Juʿfī reported from Abū ʿAmr. تُكَلِّمُ is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). وَكَهْلًا: conjoined to it; it may also be conjoined to the position. فِي الْمَهْدِ: i.e. I supported you as a small child in the cradle and as a grown man (kahl). Thābit ibn Abī Thābit reported that the kahl is one from forty to fifty years of age; others said: thirty-three years old. وَإِذْ تَخْلُقُ مِنَ الطِّينِ كَهَيْئَةِ الطَّيْرِ: the meaning of تخلق is "you shape it in an even shaping, with nothing more and nothing less". فَتَنْفُخُ فِيها فَتَكُونُ طَيْراً بِإِذْنِي: i.e. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, turns the breath that comes from the blowing into flesh and blood. It has also been read طَيْراً! [Translator's note: the variant reading (presumably طائرا) is not shown in the source.] وَتُبْرِئُ الْأَكْمَهَ وَالْأَبْرَصَ بِإِذْنِي: the meaning of بإذني is "by your supplication to Me, and I cure them". Al-Khalīl, may Allah have mercy on him, said: al-akmah is one who is born blind, and one who becomes blind after having had sight.

nahhas-irab:111-111.t: آمَنَّا وَاشْهَدْ بِأَنَّنا مُسْلِمُونَ: according to the original form; some Arabs omit one of the two nūns.

nahhas-irab:112-112.t: i.e. will He do that at our request? We have [already] mentioned it. قالَ اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ: al-Kisāʾī read هل تستطيع ربّك, i.e. "can you ask your Lord?". He said: اتّقوا الله, i.e. guard against disobeying Allah and against much asking, for you do not know what will befall you when you demand signs, since Allah, Mighty and Majestic, does only what is best for His servants. إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ: i.e. if you are believers in Him and in what I have brought, then I have brought you signs that suffice.

nahhas-irab:113-113.t: قالُوا نُرِيدُ أَنْ نَأْكُلَ مِنْها: accusative by أن. وَتَطْمَئِنَّ قُلُوبُنا وَنَعْلَمَ أَنْ قَدْ صَدَقْتَنا وَنَكُونَ عَلَيْها مِنَ الشَّاهِدِينَ: all of it is conjoined.

nahhas-irab:114-114.t:
قالَ عِيسَى ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ اللَّهُمَّ: the original form according to Sībawayh is يا الله, and the [doubled] mīm is a substitute for يا.
رَبَّنا: a second vocative; Sībawayh permits nothing else, and in his view it may not be a naʿt (adjective), because [اللهم] has come to resemble sounds (aṣwāt) on account of what has been attached to it. أَنْزِلْ عَلَيْنا مائِدَةً مِنَ السَّماءِ: a request. تَكُونُ: a naʿt of المائدة, not an answer [to the request]. Al-Aʿmash read تكن لنا عيدا, as the answer. The meaning is "the day of its descent will be a festival for us". لِأَوَّلِنا: for the first of our community and its last. ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī read لِأَوَّلِنا وَآخِرِنا. [Translator's note: the source does not show how al-Jaḥdarī's reading differs.]

nahhas-irab:115-115.t: This entails that He did send it down, and His promise is the truth.

nahhas-irab:116-116.t:
The meaning is "and when Allah will say on the Day of Resurrection". «فعل» (the past) comes in the sense of «يفعل», and «يفعل» in the sense of «فعل», when the meaning is known, because the verb is one, and it differs only because of the difference of time. Sībawayh recited, in a parallel to the verse: [al-Kāmil metre] 127-
ولقد أمرّ على اللّئيم يسبّني ... فمضيت ثمّت قلت لا يعنيني
(I pass by the base man who reviles me, and I went on, then said: "He does not mean me.")
And another said: [al-Kāmil metre] 128-
وانضح جوانب قبره بدمائها ... فلقد يكون أخا دم وذبائح
(Sprinkle the sides of his grave with their blood, for he is [i.e. was] a man of blood and slaughtered beasts.)
He means "for he was". قالَ سُبْحانَكَ: a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "declaring You far above having any god with You besides You".
ما يَكُونُ لِي أَنْ أَقُولَ ما لَيْسَ لِي بِحَقٍّ: this is the end [of the sentence]. «بحق» belongs to the ṣila of لي, and the bāʾ must be attached to (mutaʿalliq) something. تَعْلَمُ ما فِي نَفْسِي وَلا أَعْلَمُ ما فِي نَفْسِكَ: i.e. You know the truth of what is with me and I do not know the truth of what is with You — by way of pairing (izdiwāj). Al-Māzinī said: the implied form is "if it is said that I said it".

nahhas-irab:117-117.t: أَنِ: it has no grammatical position; it is explicative, like وَانْطَلَقَ الْمَلَأُ مِنْهُمْ أَنِ امْشُوا [Ṣād: 6]. «أن» may also be in the position of an accusative, i.e. "I mentioned to them only the worship of Allah, Mighty and Majestic"; and it may be in the position of a genitive, i.e. "that (بأن) [they] worship". The ḍamma on the nūn is better, because they find a kasra followed by a ḍamma heavy; the kasra is permissible according to the basic rule for the meeting of two quiescent letters. وَكُنْتُ عَلَيْهِمْ شَهِيداً ما دُمْتُ فِيهِمْ: (ما) is in the position of an accusative, i.e. "the time of my remaining among them". فَلَمَّا تَوَفَّيْتَنِي كُنْتَ أَنْتَ الرَّقِيبَ عَلَيْهِمْ: it has been said that this indicates that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, took him [in death] before raising him.

nahhas-irab:118-118.t: إِنْ تُعَذِّبْهُمْ فَإِنَّهُمْ عِبادُكَ: a condition and its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). وَإِنْ تَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ فَإِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ: likewise. Its explanation has already passed: al-ʿAzīz is the One who is not overpowered, al-Ḥakīm [the Wise] in His action.

nahhas-irab:119-119.t:
قالَ اللَّهُ هذا يَوْمُ يَنْفَعُ الصَّادِقِينَ صِدْقُهُمْ: this is the clear reading, by mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). There are two other aspects in it. One is هذا يَوْمُ يَنْفَعُ الصَّادِقِينَ صِدْقُهُمْ with tanwīn [i.e. يومٌ], with an omission in it [of فيه], like وَاتَّقُوا يَوْماً لا تَجْزِي نَفْسٌ عَنْ نَفْسٍ شَيْئاً [al-Baqara: 123]. The other aspect is هذا يَوْمُ يَنْفَعُ الصَّادِقِينَ صِدْقُهُمْ with يوم in the accusative. Ibrāhīm ibn Ḥumayd reported from Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] that this reading is not permissible, because it puts the khabar of the mubtadaʾ in the accusative. Abū Jaʿfar said: and indeclinability (bināʾ) is not permissible in it. Ibrāhīm ibn al-Sarī [al-Zajjāj] said: it is permissible, in the sense of "Allah said this to ʿĪsā on a day when their truthfulness benefits the truthful", i.e. He says it on the Day of Resurrection. Others said: the implied form is "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: these things occur on the Day of Resurrection". Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ said: «يوم» here is made indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, because it is in construct with something other than a noun, as you say مضى يومئذ; and al-Kisāʾī recited: [al-Ṭawīl metre] 129-
على حين عاتبت المشيب على الصّبا ... وقلت ألمّا تصح والشّيب وازع
(At the time when I reproached grey hair over youth, and said: "Have you not yet sobered up, when grey hair is a restrainer?")
The Basrans do not permit what the two of them said when you put the adverb in construct with an imperfect verb; if it is a past verb it is good, as occurs in the verse. Adverbs of time may be put in construct with the verb only because the verb is in the sense of the maṣdar (verbal noun). Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: the reality of the quotation (ḥikāya) … [Translator's note: the sentence breaks off here in the source.] أَبَداً: an adverb of time.

nahhas-irab:120-120.t: وَهُوَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate).
